## Goal
- Repair the IVX/Rork owner-chat QA failure where a sent user message stalls at `USER_ROW_INSERTED` and never triggers AI, then validate, commit, deploy, and verify it live.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Use GitHub repository `ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform` on `main`.
- Do not hide failures with `@ts-ignore`, broad `any`, disabled checks, `continue-on-error`, or `|| true`.
- Preserve frozen lockfile enforcement.
- Do not expose credential values or request tokens in chat.
- Avoid committing `.rork/history/main/` or generated report artifacts.
- Provide verified evidence rather than unsupported completion claims.
- Do not claim full certification while CI acceptance jobs fail or remain running.
- Do not modify members, investors, payments, properties, credentials, production data, or owner permissions.
- User wants the Rork QA issue fixed, deployed live, and verified now.

## Progress
### Done
- Audited failed workflow run #575:
  - Run ID: `30728220317`
  - Head SHA: `3f816c3b6d7ef60cb84bd5d3bd306c5a60080a8d`
  - `Lint` and `TypeScript typecheck` passed; Maestro and Playwright failed.
- Published first E2E repair commit:
  - SHA: `7bc45e3bf4855a20d6423d894ef4bb9eb436ba2b`
  - Message: `fix(e2e): restore production web coverage and valid Maestro flow`
  - Added `expo/__tests__/e2e/ivx-owner-ai-smoke.spec.ts`.
  - Changed `expo/playwright.config.ts` default `baseURL` to `https://ivxholding.com`.
  - Removed unsupported Maestro `timeout` properties from the full chat flow.
- Diagnosed workflow run #576 failures:
  - Run ID: `30728475913`
  - Maestro rejected `scroll.direction`.
  - Playwright failed due to runner/package-resolution mismatch from invocation outside Expo.
- Published and deployed follow-up E2E repair:
  - SHA: `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`
  - Message: `fix(e2e): run web tests from Expo and boot iOS before Maestro`
  - `.github/workflows/ivx-e2e.yml` runs Playwright installation and tests with `working-directory: expo`.
  - Maestro builds/launches iOS via `bunx expo run:ios --configuration debug --no-bundler` before `expo/.maestro/ivx-app-launch.yaml`.
  - Removed remaining `timeout: 30000` from `expo/.maestro/ivx-app-launch.yaml`.
- Verified live backend deployment before the current Rork fix:
  - GitHub `main`: `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`.
  - `GET https://api.ivxholding.com/health`: `healthy`, production, commit `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`.
  - `GET https://api.ivxholding.com/version`: commit `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`, `commitShort: "d1d232a6"`.
  - Public chat API returned `56` for `7 multiplied by 8`.
- Audited the owner execution implementation:
  - `backend/api/ivx-owner-ai.ts` routes authoritative owner execution intent to `executeOwnerAuthorizedDeveloperAction`.
  - `backend/services/ivx-owner-execution-mode.ts` auto-approves non-destructive owner commands and requires confirmation for dangerous actions.
  - `backend/services/ivx-senior-developer-worker.ts` implements patch → validation → commit → deploy → production verification.
- Ran focused backend worker/dev-mode tests:
  - `bun test ./backend/ivx-senior-developer-worker.test.ts ./backend/services/ivx-owner-ai-dev-mode.test.ts`
  - Passed tests shown, including owner approval gating, queue attachment behavior, cancellation/resume, and proof summarization.
  - Test output included non-fatal local Supabase `HTTP 401` emergency-stop read warnings.
- Diagnosed the Rork IVX Chat QA report:
  - The symptom is a watchdog timeout after optimistic user-row insertion, before `AI_TRIGGER_DECISION` / `AI_MUTATION_STARTED`.
  - In `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`, local-first `send_and_ai` awaited `sendQueue.mutateAsync(...)` before invoking `assistantReplyMutation`.
  - `chatTransportQueue` can retry persistence; therefore a durable-persistence delay could strand the valid optimistic message at `USER_ROW_INSERTED`.
- Implemented the targeted local-first trigger repair:
  - Added `expo/src/modules/chat/services/ivxSendTriggerPolicy.ts`.
  - Added `expo/__tests__/ivx-send-trigger-policy.test.ts`.
  - Modified `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx` so local-first `send_and_ai` / `ai_only` starts `assistantReplyMutation` immediately while durable user-message persistence continues in the background.
  - Preserved persistence-first behavior for `send_only` and `attachment`.
  - Preserved elevated-confirmation handling before AI execution.
  - Added watchdog detail identifying whether persistence is `background` or `confirmed`.
- Ran focused Expo tests:
  - `cd expo && bun test __tests__/ivx-send-trigger-policy.test.ts __tests__/ivx-owner-ai-orchestrator.test.ts __tests__/ivx-watchdog.test.ts`
  - Passed output included owner-AI orchestrator lifecycle tests and watchdog tests; the new trigger-policy test was included in the command.
- Ran Expo lint:
  - `cd expo && bun run lint`
  - Completed with existing warnings; no lint error was reported.

### In Progress
- Validate the current local-first AI-trigger repair completely:
  - The `cd expo && bunx tsc --noEmit` command exceeded the 60-second tool timeout and needs rerun with sufficient time or narrowed diagnosis.
  - Confirm focused test command’s final exit/result after truncated tool output if needed.
- Inspect Git diff, ensure only the intended three Expo files changed, then commit and push the Rork QA repair.
- Trigger/poll GitHub Actions for the repair commit.
- Deploy the final commit through the approved production flow and verify `/health`, `/version`, and SHA parity.
- Verify the UI behavior in an actual Rork/Expo runtime because `rork-agent logs runtime --errors` and `rork-agent logs backend --limit 100` returned no logs for this project.
- Workflow run #577 remains last-known in progress:
  - Run ID: `30728658851`
  - URL: `https://github.com/ibb142/ivx-holdings-platform/actions/runs/30728658851`
  - Head SHA: `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`
  - TypeScript, Lint, and Playwright succeeded.
  - Maestro E2E was still in progress at last poll.

### Blocked
- The current Rork QA repair has not yet been committed, pushed, deployed, or production-verified.
- Full mobile CI certification remains blocked until Maestro run #577 completes successfully or is repaired from its actual result.
- No Rork runtime/backend logs were available:
  - `rork-agent logs runtime --errors | rg -i 'ivx|watchdog|trigger|sendmessage|timeout'` → `No runtime logs found for this project.`
  - `rork-agent logs backend --limit 100 | rg -i 'owner-ai|watchdog|error|timeout|trigger'` → `No backend logs found for this project.`
- Authenticated owner-only backend execution cannot be invoked from this workspace merely because the user is signed in on a separate device/browser; no session credential is accessible in the tool context.

## Key Decisions
- Fix the proven stalled checkpoint rather than changing unrelated owner-execution, persistence, or production-data behavior.
- For local-first `send_and_ai` and `ai_only`, start the assistant request from the already-visible optimistic user row; let persistence retry independently.
- Keep `send_only` and attachment flows persistence-first because they do not require an immediate assistant response.
- Preserve the elevated-confirmation gate before starting AI, even in local-first mode.
- Add a pure trigger-policy helper and unit tests so the critical persistence/AI ordering is directly testable without mounting `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`.
- Keep Bun `1.3.9` in `.github/workflows/ivx-e2e.yml` and preserve `--frozen-lockfile`.
- Run Playwright from `expo` so CLI and imported `@playwright/test` use the same dependency context.
- Treat GitHub `main` SHA equality with `/health` and `/version` SHA as production deployment evidence.

## Next Steps
1. Rerun `cd expo && bunx tsc --noEmit` with adequate runtime and repair any actual diagnostics.
2. Rerun/confirm focused tests, including `expo/__tests__/ivx-send-trigger-policy.test.ts`, and inspect the complete result.
3. Inspect `git diff --check` and changed files; ensure the patch is limited to:
   - `expo/app/ivx/chat.tsx`
   - `expo/src/modules/chat/services/ivxSendTriggerPolicy.ts`
   - `expo/__tests__/ivx-send-trigger-policy.test.ts`
4. Commit the Rork QA trigger repair on a dedicated branch, push it, and open/merge through the approved flow.
5. Poll workflow run #577; if Maestro fails, inspect its log and fix the real simulator/flow defect without weakening CI.
6. Run GitHub Actions for the new repair SHA and require TypeScript, lint, Playwright, and Maestro success.
7. Deploy the merged final SHA through the approved production flow.
8. Verify `https://api.ivxholding.com/health` and `https://api.ivxholding.com/version`, then compare GitHub SHA = Render/deploy SHA = runtime SHA.
9. Verify in the Rork/Expo app that a local-first owner chat send proceeds from `USER_ROW_INSERTED` through `AI_TRIGGER_DECISION` and `AI_MUTATION_STARTED` without watchdog timeout.

## Critical Context
- Current production SHA before the Rork QA repair: `d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7`.
- Current production `/health`:

  - `environment: "production"`
  - `commit: "d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7"`

  - `commit: "d1d232a65328a4a045644d838b5014a1c74e0ef7"`

- Local-first mode is explicitly enabled only when `EXPO_PUBLIC_IVX_CHAT_BACKEND_MODE` is `local`, `local_first`, or `offline`; otherwise `ivxLocalFirstRuntime.ts` defaults to `remote_first`.
- The repair applies only when `localFirstChatMode` is true; remote-first behavior is unchanged.
- `sendQueue.mutateAsync(...)` uses the durable `chatTransportQueue`, which has retries, timeouts, and queue state; waiting for it can delay AI dispatch beyond the watchdog’s timeout.
- Watchdog checkpoints are ordered:
  - `SEND_TAP`

- The TypeScript command result was not a compiler failure; the execution tool returned `Command timed out after 60 seconds.`

  - Maestro: `Unknown Property: direction at /Users/runner/work/ivx-holdings-platform/ivx-holdings-platform/expo/.maestro/ivx-chat-qa-full.yaml:39:1`
  - Playwright: `Error: Playwright Test did not expect test.describe() to be called here.`

     3|Use this playbook when an app builds successfully but the user reports that runtime behavior is still wrong, especially with vague feedback like "it doesn't work", "still broken", "the tap does nothing", or "the screen does not change".
     4|
     5|This applies across React Native, React web, SwiftUI, and Kotlin apps. A successful build only proves the code compiles; it does not prove the user event reached the app, state changed, the relevant UI is mounted, or side effects and permissions are aligned.
     6|
     7|## Core Rule
     8|
     9|Classify the failure before editing again. Work from the furthest confirmed point in the flow:
    10|
    11|- **Launch/build**: The app installs and opens without crashing.
    12|- **Event delivery**: The tap, notification response, deep link, delegate callback, router event, or async completion fires.
    13|- **State mutation**: The expected React state, store value, observable model, navigation path, permission state, or view model property changes.
    14|- **Render/presentation**: The destination component/view is mounted by the active route, root view, navigator, sheet, modal, full-screen cover, overlay, or conditional branch.
    15|- **Side effects**: Audio, haptics, network calls, logs, notifications, storage writes, or other non-visual effects happen.
    16|
    17|If a later checkpoint is confirmed, do not keep rewriting earlier layers. Move forward to the next unproven checkpoint.
    18|
    19|## Vague User Feedback
    20|
    21|When the user only says the behavior is still broken, ask one focused follow-up if no observable signal exists. Separate the checkpoints:
    22|
    23|- Does the app open?
    24|- Does any sound, log, haptic, notification, network call, or other side effect happen?
    25|- Does any screen or visible state change?

     3| *
     4| * PROBLEM (owner directive 2026-07-25): the owner asked "Audit the loading
     5| * problem on this chat, explain what is wrong, what must be fixed, and deploy
     6| * it." This is a DIAGNOSTIC request, but the old `isSeniorDeveloperBuildRequest`
     7| * matcher caught the word "deploy it" and misrouted the entire message to the
     8| * Senior Developer Worker — which returned task-progress percentages (RUNNING
     9| * 10%, COMMITTING 65%) instead of a diagnosis.
    10| *
    11| * This classifier runs BEFORE the build-intent check and separates:
    12| *
    13| *   A. DIAGNOSTIC  — "audit", "why is X failing", "diagnose", "explain what is wrong"
    14| *   B. CODE_CHANGE — "fix the bug", "change the code", "add a feature"
    15| *   C. DEPLOYMENT  — "deploy this", "ship to production", "push to main"
    16| *   D. STATUS      — "what is the task status", "show me the progress"
    17| *   E. EXPLANATION — "explain the architecture", "how does X work"
    18| *
    19| * Diagnostic, status, and explanation requests must NEVER be routed to the
    20| * worker. Only explicit code-change and deployment requests (without a
    21| * diagnostic lead) trigger the worker flow.
    22| *
    23| * Pure + deterministic (no I/O, no AI) so it is fully unit-testable.
    24| */
    25|
    26|export type OwnerIntentClass =
    27|  | 'diagnostic'
    28|  | 'code_change'
    29|  | 'deployment'
    30|  | 'status'
    31|  | 'explanation';
    32|
    33|export type OwnerIntentClassification = {
    34|  intent: OwnerIntentClass;
    35|  /** True when this message should route to the Senior Developer Worker. */
    36|  routesToWorker: boolean;
    37|  /** True when this message is a diagnostic request that needs a real analysis. */
    38|  isDiagnostic: boolean;
    39|  /** The specific subject/module the diagnostic targets (e.g. "chat loading"). */
    40|  diagnosticSubject: string | null;
    41|  /** Brief reason for the classification (for audit logging). */
    42|  reason: string;
    43|};
    44|
    45|/**
    46| * Diagnostic lead patterns. When a message BEGINS with or is structured as a
    47| * diagnostic request, it is classified as DIAGNOSTIC regardless of whether it
    48| * also mentions "deploy" or "fix" later. The diagnostic intent takes priority.
    49| *
    50| * Matches:
    51| *   - "Audit the loading problem on this chat"
    52| *   - "Why is member registration failing?"
    53| *   - "Diagnose the chat cold-start issue"
    54| *   - "Explain what is wrong with the chat"
    55| *   - "What is broken in the reels screen"
    56| *   - "Audit chat loading and deploy it" (diagnostic with deploy suffix)
    57| */
    58|const DIAGNOSTIC_LEAD_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [
    59|  /\b(?:audit|diagnose|investigate|analyze|analyse)\b/i,
    60|  /\bwhy\s+(?:is|are|does|do|can|cannot|can't|won't|doesn't|don't|did|didn't|has|have|hasn't|haven't)\b/i,
    61|  /\bwhat\s+(?:is|are)\s+(?:wrong|broken|failing|the\s+problem|the\s+issue|the\s+cause)\b/i,
    62|  /\bexplain\s+what\s+is\s+wrong\b/i,
    63|  /\b(?:find|identify)\s+the\s+(?:root\s+cause|problem|issue|failure)\b/i,
    64|  /\breproduce\s+the\s+(?:failure|bug|issue|error)\b/i,
    65|  /\bloading\s+problem\b/i,
    66|  /\bcold[-\s]?start\s+(?:problem|issue|failure)\b/i,
    67|];
    68|
    69|/**
    70| * Status request patterns. These return task/progress status, not diagnosis.
    71| */
    72|const STATUS_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [
    73|  /\b(?:what\s+is|show\s+me|give\s+me)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:task\s+)?status\b/i,
    74|  /\b(?:task|job|worker)\s+status\b/i,
    75|  /\bwhat\s+(?:is|are)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:progress|results?|findings?)\b/i,
    76|  /\bshow\s+(?:me\s+)?(?:the\s+)?(?:progress|status|results?)\b/i,
    77|  /\bwhat\s+(?:is|'s|is)\s+happening\b/i,
    78|  /\b(?:is|are)\s+(?:it|the\s+(?:task|job|worker|deploy))\s+(?:still\s+)?(?:running|done|complete|finished)\b/i,
    79|];
    80|
    81|/**
    82| * Explanation request patterns. These ask for architectural understanding,
    83| * not a diagnosis or code change.
    84| */
    85|const EXPLANATION_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [
    86|  /\bexplain\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:architecture|design|system|how|what)\b/i,
    87|  /\bhow\s+does\s+.+\bwork\b/i,
    88|  /\bdescribe\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:architecture|system|design|structure)\b/i,
    89|  /\bwalk\s+me\s+through\b/i,
    90|  /\b(?:what\s+is|tell\s+me\s+about)\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:architecture|design|system|stack)\b/i,
    91|];
    92|
    93|/**
    94| * Deployment request patterns — explicit deploy/ship/push without a diagnostic lead.
    95| */
    96|const DEPLOYMENT_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [
    97|  /\bdeploy\s+(?:this|it|the\s+app|the\s+build|to\s+production|now)\b/i,
    98|  /\bship\s+(?:this|it|to\s+production)\b/i,
    99|  /\bpush\s+to\s+(?:production|github|main)\b/i,
   100|  /\bgo\s+live\b/i,
   101|  /\brelease\s+(?:this|it|the\s+app|to\s+production)\b/i,
   102|];
   103|
   104|/**
   105| * Code-change request patterns — explicit code modification without a
   106| * diagnostic lead. These are imperative build/fix/change instructions.
   107| */
   108|const CODE_CHANGE_PATTERNS: RegExp[] = [
   109|  /\bfix\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:bug|issue|error|crash|defect)\b/i,
   110|  /\b(?:bug\s*fix|hotfix)\b/i,
   111|  /\bpatch\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:bug|code|file|issue)\b/i,
   112|  /\brepair\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:bug|code|issue)\b/i,
   113|  /\bbuild\s+(?:an?\s+)?(?:(?:new|complete|full|whole)\s+)?(?:app|module|feature|endpoint|screen|page|service|api|component)\b/i,
   114|  /\bcreate\s+(?:an?\s+)?(?:(?:new|complete|full|whole)\s+)?(?:app|module|feature|endpoint|screen|page|service|api|component|function)\b/i,
   115|  /\b(?:add|implement)\s+(?:an?\s+)?(?:(?:new|complete|full|whole)\s+)?(?:feature|endpoint|screen|page|service|api|component|function)\b/i,
   116|  /\bmodify\s+(?:the\s+)?code\b/i,
   117|  /\bchange\s+(?:the\s+)?code\b/i,
   118|  /\brefactor\b/i,
   119|  /\brewrite\b/i,
   120|];
   121|
   122|/**
   123| * Extract the diagnostic subject from the message (e.g. "chat loading" from
   124| * "Audit the loading problem on this chat").
   125| */
   126|function extractDiagnosticSubject(message: string): string | null {
   127|  const text = message.trim();
   128|
   129|  // "chat loading" / "loading problem on this chat"
   130|  const chatLoadingMatch = text.match(/\b(chat\s+)?(?:loading|cold[-\s]?start|startup)\s+(?:problem|issue|failure|error|slow|delay)\b/i);
   131|  if (chatLoadingMatch) {
   132|    return 'chat loading';
   133|  }
   134|
   135|  // "chat" generically
   136|  if (/\bchat\b/i.test(text) && /\b(?:loading|cold|startup|render|blank|frozen|spinner|stuck)\b/i.test(text)) {
   137|    return 'chat loading';
   138|  }
   139|
   140|  // "member registration"

   142|  if (registrationMatch) {
   143|    return 'member registration';
   144|  }
   145|
   146|  // "reels crashing"
   147|  const reelsMatch = text.match(/\breels?\s+(?:crashing|broken|failing|error|problem)\b/i);

   150|  }
   151|
   152|  // Generic "X is failing/broken"
   153|  const genericMatch = text.match(/\b(\w+(?:\s+\w+)?)\s+(?:is\s+)?(?:failing|broken|crashing|not\s+working|erroring)\b/i);
   154|  if (genericMatch) {
   155|    return genericMatch[1].toLowerCase();
   156|  }
   157|
   158|  return null;
   159|}
   160|
   161|/**
   162| * Classify an owner chat message into one of 5 intent classes.
   163| *
   164| * Priority order:
   165| *   1. DIAGNOSTIC — if the message has a diagnostic lead, it is diagnostic
   166| *      regardless of trailing "deploy" or "fix" words.
   167| *   2. STATUS — task/progress status requests.
   168| *   3. EXPLANATION — architecture/design questions.
   169| *   4. DEPLOYMENT — explicit deploy/ship without diagnostic lead.
   170| *   5. CODE_CHANGE — explicit fix/build/change without diagnostic lead.
   171| *
   172| * Only DEPLOYMENT and CODE_CHANGE route to the worker.
   173| */
   174|export function classifyOwnerIntent(message: string): OwnerIntentClassification {
   175|  const text = message.trim();
   176|  if (text.length === 0) {
   177|    return {
   178|      intent: 'explanation',
   179|      routesToWorker: false,
   180|      isDiagnostic: false,
   181|      diagnosticSubject: null,
   182|      reason: 'empty message — defaulting to explanation',
   183|    };
   184|  }
   185|
   186|  // 1. DIAGNOSTIC — highest priority, takes precedence over deploy/fix
   187|  if (DIAGNOSTIC_LEAD_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(text))) {
   188|    const subject = extractDiagnosticSubject(text);

   190|      intent: 'diagnostic',
   191|      routesToWorker: false,
   192|      isDiagnostic: true,
   193|      diagnosticSubject: subject,

   195|    };
   196|  }
   197|
   198|  // 2. STATUS
   199|  if (STATUS_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(text))) {
   200|    return {
   201|      intent: 'status',
   202|      routesToWorker: false,
   203|      isDiagnostic: false,
   204|      diagnosticSubject: null,
   205|      reason: 'status request detected',
   206|    };
   207|  }
   208|
   209|  // 3. EXPLANATION
   210|  if (EXPLANATION_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(text))) {
   211|    return {
   212|      intent: 'explanation',
   213|      routesToWorker: false,
   214|      isDiagnostic: false,
   215|      diagnosticSubject: null,
   216|      reason: 'explanation request detected',
   217|    };
   218|  }
   219|
   220|  // 4. DEPLOYMENT
   221|  if (DEPLOYMENT_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(text))) {
   222|    return {
   223|      intent: 'deployment',
   224|      routesToWorker: true,
   225|      isDiagnostic: false,
   226|      diagnosticSubject: null,
   227|      reason: 'explicit deployment request',
   228|    };
   229|  }
   230|
   231|  // 5. CODE_CHANGE
   232|  if (CODE_CHANGE_PATTERNS.some((pattern) => pattern.test(text))) {
   233|    return {
   234|      intent: 'code_change',
   235|      routesToWorker: true,
   236|      isDiagnostic: false,
   237|      diagnosticSubject: null,
   238|      reason: 'explicit code-change request',
   239|    };
   240|  }
   241|
   242|  // Default: conversational/explanation
   243|  return {
   244|    intent: 'explanation',
   245|    routesToWorker: false,
   246|    isDiagnostic: false,
   247|    diagnosticSubject: null,
   248|    reason: 'no specific intent pattern matched — defaulting to explanation',
   249|  };
   250|}

   253| * Quick boolean: is this a diagnostic request?
   254| */
   255|export function isDiagnosticRequest(message: string): boolean {
